back: The values that separate classes with no gaps, e.g. 24.5 and 29.5 for the whole-number class 25–29.
$\text{frequency density} = \dfrac{\text{frequency}}{\text{class width}}$; in a histogram, area of a bar = frequency.
Running totals plotted at upper class boundaries, starting at 0 at the first lower boundary; joined by a smooth curve.
Frequencies plotted at class midpoints and joined with straight lines; good for comparing distributions.
Keeps every value: stems (e.g. tens) and ordered leaves (units), with a key such as 5 | 3 = 53.
Qualitative: bar or pie chart. Continuous grouped: histogram, frequency polygon, cumulative frequency curve.
Short, clear, neutral; tick boxes that do not overlap and cover every possible answer.
Questionnaire, interview, observation, experiment, existing records.
